L01.why: Absolute phrase before a main clause normally needs a closing comma; but a gerund-subject reading could survive.

L02.why: Likely run-together clauses, but an introductory phrase like 'In a panic the crowd' tolerates no comma.

L03.why: 'would of' is never standard; 'would had' is also ungrammatical in any sentence.

L04.why: Pure tense/number choice; depends entirely on subject and time frame.

L05.why: Conjunction plus verb could break parallel structure, but any form could fit some frame.

L06.why: Added subject may create comma splice, but each form is viable in some sentence.

L07.why: Number change odd one out; punctuation choice depends on sentence.

L08.why: No punctuation before a 'how' clause after 'impressions' is rarely grammatical, but not impossible.

L09.why: Single comma separates compound subject from its verb; wrong in any sentence. C/D depend on possible earlier head noun.

L10.why: Contraction likely confused with possessive, but 'it's' can be correct.

L11.why: Participle may leave no finite verb, but could work as modifier.

L12.why: Nominalized possessive likely dangling-modifier distractor, but any could be correct depending on preceding modifier.

L13.why: Agreement depends on head noun (rivers vs a singular earlier noun); none rejectable.

L14.why: Lie/lay confusion likely, but 'laid' is correct if an object follows.

L15.why: Relative pronoun may create fragment; all depend on sentence.

L17.why: Comma splits subject from verb; plural 'relays' with 'trips' disagrees. C survives as subjunctive.

L18.why: Inserted 'however' may splice clauses, but each could fit.

L19.why: Comma may splice clauses, but 'frame, three...' could be an appositive list.

L20.why: Comma after 'but' looks wrong, though possible before an intervening clause.

L21.why: Could create run-on, but a 'that' clause can be fine.

L22.why: Semicolon before 'whether' usually leaves fragment, but a whether-clause can be a subject.

L23.why: Choice hinges on the modifier's referent in the withheld sentence; no option is ungrammatical alone.

L24.why: Wordy clause likely breaks parallelism, but correctness depends on the series.
